answer: You can stop hospice care at any time if you change your mind. Your hospice provider will ask you to sign a form that includes the date your care will end, and you should not sign or date any forms until the actual date you want your care to stop.

gold_answer: They must file a written document with the hospice that includes a signed statement revoking hospice coverage for the rest of that election period and the effective date, which cannot be earlier than the date the revocation is made. A verbal revocation is not accepted, and remaining days in that election period are forfeited.
gold_quote: To revoke the election of hospice care, the individual must file a document with the hospice that includes: • A signed statement that the individual revokes the election for Medicare coverage of hospice care for the remainder of that election period, and • The effective date of that revocation. An individual may not designate an effective date earlier than the date that the revocation is made. Note that a verbal revocation of benefits is NOT acceptable. The individual forfeits hospice coverage for any remaining days in that election period.

judge.rationale: The answer captures the core requirement of signing a form with the end date, but it omits several details in the gold answer: verbal revocation is not accepted, the effective date cannot be earlier than the revocation date, and any remaining days in that election period are forfeited; every claim it does make is stated in P1.
